hypothesis: c8a is an EPYC 9R45 (Zen 5) but the family builds with -C target-cpu=znver4, so codegen targets Zen 4 and sha3-asm picks its AVX-512VL keccak; with znver5 it picks the scalar x86_64 keccak, which its author benchmarked faster on Zen 5 (keccak is ~19% of heavy-phase CPU). Expect a few % on heavy, light flat.
llm_commentary: Building c8a (EPYC 9R45, Zen 5) for znver5 instead of the family's znver4 is neutral: 4.67s [4.62-4.73] → 4.65s [4.63/4.74/4.59]. Correction to an earlier version of this note: the on-box log shows sha3-asm switching to its scalar keccak, but sha3-asm is not on reth's keccak path. alloy-primitives hashes through keccak-asm 0.1.9, whose compile-time backend (src/backend/mod.rs:14-31) picks AVX-512VL Rust intrinsics on both znver4 and znver5 and only falls back to sha3-asm on targets without AVX2/NEON. So this run measures Zen 5 codegen alone, with keccak unchanged, and finds no gain. The family flag should still be znver5 to match the hardware. Testing a different keccak backend on Zen 5 needs a keccak-asm change, not a flag.
